caption:
Pi updates can break your extensions.
This system maintains those add-ons for you.

Two lead agents assign work to delegates:
specialists who fix or review an extension.

Fixer delegates edit their extension’s copy.
Reviewer delegates check the work.

Reviewers approve or reject code changes.
They also judge questions for you.

The main fixer chooses what happens next:
release, return or hold.

Release moves approved work forward.
Product changes still need your separate push tap.

A return sends work back for revision.
The next review sees the reasons too.

After three returns, both delegates write
handoffs: notes for their replacements.

A hold waits for a named answer.
The main fixer can ask you directly.

Telegram asks one question at a time.
Your answer is handled before the next.

Late answers reach the current main fixer.
A retired delegate is replaced, with notes.

A run groups maintenance work. Usage limits
pause it without replacing the agents.

Programs restart when work arrives.
Saved conversations preserve the agents’ memory.

The first trial must discard two old patches.
Pi 1.4 already fixes their problem.

The team extension still helps Pi 1.3 users.
Removing that extra fix needs your choice.

The first version is built, but switched off.
Automatic crash recovery comes later.

Bend checks design rules, called laws,
against a simplified model of the system.

Its 52 checks cover the model, not the code.
You still need to approve those rules.

First choice: two items go back to one delegate.
Does that spend one return, or two?

Counting once saves a retry for the delegate.
The build counts each item separately.

Second choice: the system refuses
a forbidden action. What happens next?

The build pauses, notifies you, then retries.
You have not approved that failure policy.

Third choice: GitHub changes after a review.
Pushing the old patch is blocked.

The build updates the copy before retrying.
A new product patch needs another review and tap.

Fourth choice: withdrawing a held question
can leave it able to reappear. How should it close?

Dropping could close any obsolete item.
Wider withdrawal could close unreleased questions.

Or close old held items when a new run starts.
New delegates would reconsider the work.

Choose the policies and review the rules.
Then decide whether to start the live trial.
